- Material gap: the annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended February 1, 2026 and the results release for that year are not supplied. Both quarterly reports refer to that annual report and carry its year-end balance sheet as a comparative, but no annual income statement, cash flow statement or Adjusted EBITDA for fiscal 2025 appears in any supplied document, and a search of every source for fiscal 2025, trailing and twelve-month figures found none. Trailing twelve-month leverage, coverage and cash conversion are therefore not calculable, and fiscal 2025 comparisons are limited to the balance sheet. The minimum remedy is that annual report. Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C4 - Material gap: no executed financing document is supplied. The term loan credit agreement with its sixth and seventh amendments, the asset-based credit agreement with its latest amendment, and the indenture and first supplemental indenture for the 2034 notes appear only as exhibit references, and the run settings state that no legal documents were supplied. Covenant definitions, guarantor and security terms and the exact repricing terms can therefore be read only from the filings' own summaries. The minimum remedy is those agreements. Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48; 10-Q_2026-05-03_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 42 - Minor gap: no third-quarter material is supplied. The latest balance sheet is dated August 2, 2026 and the latest document September 9, 2026, while the third quarter of fiscal 2026 ends on November 1, 2026 on the company's 13-week calendar, so any later financing, repurchase or trading change is not visible. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 12 - Minor gap: no credit rating level, agency or outlook and no market price for any instrument is supplied. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view

rows.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view — paragraph 1
Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- High severity: The annual statements for fiscal 2025 (the year ended February 1, 2026) are not supplied, so the income statement and cash flow columns for fiscal 2025 are absent, no trailing twelve-month EBITDA, cash interest, revenue or operating cash flow can be built, and leverage and interest cover at fiscal 2025 and at August 2, 2026 are not calculable. The action that would close it is the annual report for that year. Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation LT1 - Medium severity: Lines that the statements print only in some periods, or print as a dash, are shown as not supplied in the other periods and are not read as zero: other expense, acquisitions, investment in tax advantaged limited partnerships, borrowings and repayments on the revolver, issuance of long-term debt, debt issuance costs, and other investing and financing items. This restricts nothing beyond those lines, because the totals tie, and no action is needed beyond reading the dash as not stated. Basis: 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8 - Medium severity: Revolver availability and letters of credit at February 1, 2026 are not stated, so undrawn committed facilities for fiscal 2025 are not supplied, and the principal debt at that date is not stated. The action that would close it is the annual report for the year ended February 1, 2026. Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 36 - Medium severity: Cumulative leverage in the debt stack is not supplied for any facility because no trailing twelve-month EBITDA denominator exists; the amounts and ranks are stated. The action that would close it is the fiscal 2025 annual report, which would allow a trailing twelve-month figure. Basis: calculation LT1 - Medium severity: The cash flow statement shows issuance of long-term debt of USD 929 million and repayments of USD 617 million in the six months ended August 2, 2026, which are not the new USD 800 million term loan and USD 750 million of notes, and the quarterly report does not reconcile them; the net change in principal ties but the gross flows should not be read as instrument amounts. The action that would close it is the issuer's reconciliation of the refinancing, which the executed amendment and indenture would give. Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 16, 18 - Medium severity: Carrying values by instrument are not disclosed in the quarterly report, so the net unamortized discount and issuance costs of USD 29 million at August 2, 2026 is derived as carrying value less principal; it restricts the instrument-level carrying values, which are not supplied. The action that would close it is the debt note of the annual report for the year ended February 1, 2026 or the third-quarter report. Basis: calculation RC1; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 19 - Low severity: Maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not disclosed, so only total capital expenditure is used in free cash flow; interest income, exceptional items, restricted cash, finance lease liabilities, supplier finance arrangements and a separate second-quarter cash flow statement are not presented in the statements and notes searched, so none is stated and the second-quarter cash flow columns are omitted. No action closes this from the issuer's public statements. Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 8 - Low severity: The lien priority between the revolving facility and the term loans, and the guarantors of the credit facilities, are not stated in the supplied filings, so the debt stack ranks secured debt together and the unsecured notes behind it without a ranking between the secured facilities. The action that would close it is the credit agreements. Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 19; EX99.1_2026-05-03_cnm_jun2026seniornoteslaunchpr-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1 - Low severity: The repricing of the 2031 Senior Term Loan is dated only as August 2026 in the subsequent-events note and the repurchases after quarter end carry no day, so the post-balance-sheet rows state no day and no principal effect for the repricing. The action that would close it is the third-quarter report. Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 23; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1 - Low severity: The company reports one operating segment and no corporate or eliminations line, so no segment sum is stated beyond the product-category net sales, whose meter category is reported as smart utility products in the 2026 documents without a stated link between them. The action that would close it is the issuer's own mapping of the two labels. Basis: 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 13 - Low severity: The covenant ratio that governs excess cash flow repayment, a secured leverage ratio of 3.25 or more, and the fixed charge coverage test are defined in agreements that are not supplied and no reported covenant figure is stated, although the quarterly report states compliance with all debt covenants at August 2, 2026, so covenant capacity is not inferred. The action that would close it is the credit agreements and the issuer's reported covenant figures. Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 19

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: No sponsor controls Core & Main, so no sponsor-driven distribution or sponsor equity support is documented in either direction. CD&R, the former sponsor, sold down through secondary offerings, seven of them between April 2023 and January 2024, and held no Class A or Class B shares from January 25, 2024. The company bought 28.05% of the shares those sellers disposed of in fiscal 2023, for USD 1,344 million. What remains is a classified board, Class A shares that are in many cases held through brokers and institutions (three holders of record at February 2, 2025) and the management holding vehicle's 3.30% of the combined Class A and Class B shares, held as Class B; larger current holders are not established because the proxy statement is not supplied. Basis: calculation SE1; calculation SE2; calculation SE3; calculation SE4; calculation OW5; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 68, 75, 110

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case for lower risk is that the structure has been handled prudently: the company has no approved dividend plan, the revolver was undrawn at February 1, 2026 and August 2, 2026, three term loan repricings since May 2024 have cut the margin, final maturities now start in 2031, and the quarterly report states compliance with all debt covenants. If fiscal 2026 buybacks and tax receivable payments are met from operating cash flow rather than new term debt and the next annual report shows principal falling, the view would move to low. It would move to high if a new controlling holder appears, if the credit agreements show wide restricted-payment capacity that the company uses for larger debt-funded buybacks, if tax receivable payments accelerate, or if any amendment subordinates or releases lenders. Basis: 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 75, 79, 128; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 19, 23

facts.text: Business risk is moderate: customers are highly diversified and capital needs are low, but demand follows construction. facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Core & Main distributes water, wastewater, storm drainage and fire protection products and related services to municipalities, private water companies and professional contractors through over 370 branches in the United States and Canada, selling more than 225,000 products from more than 5,000 suppliers to more than 60,000 customers. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Core & Main presents an adequate business profile supported by customer diversification, low capital needs and USD 1,538 million of liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by shareholder returns above free cash flow, USD 685 million of tax receivable claims and a leverage measure that can be fixed only to fiscal 2024. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because operating cash flow was 117.47% and 66.77% of Adjusted EBITDA in the last two fiscal years, although the first half is seasonally weak. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the leverage trend ahead of fiscal 2030, since no maturity falls before February 2031. The primary downside path is a construction downturn met with unchanged shareholder returns, which would raise leverage while liquidity holds. Against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector the business profile cannot be compared, because no peer data is supplied. Further analysis would require the annual report for fiscal 2025, the third-quarter report, the credit agreements and a rating or peer set. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: debt-funded shareholder returns ahead of a construction downturn. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Debt of USD 2,449 million is backed by USD 1,538 million of cash and revolver availability, but leverage and interest cover can be stated only for fiscal 2023 and 2024, because the annual report for the year ended February 1, 2026 is missing.
Basis: calculation TD5; calculation LQ1; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 11

On balance-sheet carrying value, net debt was USD 2,137 million at August 2, 2026, below USD 2,253 million at the end of fiscal 2024, when it was 2.49x reported EBITDA, even though the company repurchased USD 257 million of shares in the first half of fiscal 2026 and raised USD 293 million of net new debt. A further USD 11 million of repurchases after the quarter end lifts pro forma net debt to USD 2,148 million.
Basis: calculation ND5; calculation ND2; calculation LV2; calculation DF1; calculation PB1; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1
Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 8.47x in fiscal 2023 and 4.59x in fiscal 2024; no later cover ratio can be stated.
Basis: calculation CV1; calculation CV2
### Key findings

Net debt on carrying value rose from USD 1,877 million at the end of fiscal 2023 to USD 2,253 million at the end of fiscal 2024, taking net debt to reported EBITDA from 2.11x to 2.49x, because acquisitions of USD 741 million and share repurchases of USD 176 million were funded beside operating cash flow of USD 621 million. Net debt then fell to USD 1,928 million at the end of fiscal 2025 and rose by USD 209 million to USD 2,137 million by August 2, 2026, as USD 257 million of share repurchases and USD 42 million of tax receivable agreement payments outweighed free cash flow of USD 112 million. The direction since fiscal 2024 is lower, but no ratio can be stated for the later dates.

Basis: calculation ND1; calculation ND2; calculation ND3; calculation ND5; calculation NC1; calculation NC3; calculation FC4; calculation LV1; calculation LV2; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 8

Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 4.59x in fiscal 2024 against 8.47x in fiscal 2023, because interest expense rose from USD 81 million to USD 142 million after the acquisitions and larger borrowings, and cash interest paid rose from USD 105 million to USD 197 million. In the first half of fiscal 2026 cash interest paid was USD 59 million against USD 49 million while interest expense eased from USD 61 million to USD 59 million; without trailing twelve-month EBITDA the current cover ratio is not established.
Basis: calculation CV1; calculation CV2; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 106, 108; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8

Liquidity at August 2, 2026 was USD 1,538 million: USD 312 million of cash and about USD 1,226 million of availability under the undrawn USD 1,250 million revolver, which depends on the borrowing base; an April 2026 amendment extended its maturity from 2029 to 2031. The July 2026 refinancing replaced the 2028 term loan with a USD 800 million term loan due 2033 and USD 750 million of senior notes due 2034, so scheduled principal is only USD 17 million a year until the USD 928 million term loan falls due in 2031.
Basis: calculation LQ1; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 18, 19, 36

Operating cash flow was USD 144 million in the first half of fiscal 2026 against USD 111 million, after working capital absorbed USD 242 million (USD 255 million a year earlier), and free cash flow after USD 32 million of capital expenditure was USD 112 million. Share repurchases and tax receivable agreement payments of USD 299 million exceeded that by USD 187 million, and net new debt of USD 293 million covered the gap, so shareholder returns in the half were partly debt-funded.
Basis: calculation FC4; calculation FC3; calculation WC1; calculation WC2; calculation SR1; calculation SR2; calculation DF1; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 8

Outside debt, the balance sheet carries USD 644 million of tax receivable agreement liabilities, whose cash payments were USD 42 million in the first half against USD 18 million, USD 300 million of operating lease liabilities and USD 1,223 million of supplier purchase obligations that are generally cancellable; none is in the debt or net debt figures.
Basis: calculation LS1; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 40

Reported EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are the issuer's own figures, with add-backs of USD 25 million in fiscal 2024, so the choice of measure moves net leverage by only 0.07x; depreciation and amortization is stated as USD 183 million, USD 186 million and USD 194 million on three bases in fiscal 2024, and fiscal 2024 had 53 weeks.
Basis: calculation AB1; calculation LV2; calculation LV3; calculation LV4; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 97, 106, 108
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against reading the lower net debt as deleveraging is seasonality and funding: working capital absorbed USD 242 million in the half and part of the repurchases was debt-funded, so the year-end balance for fiscal 2026 could look different from the August balance. The case for stability is that the revolver was undrawn at August 2, 2026 and at the end of fiscal 2025, and the earliest bullet maturity is in 2031. A fiscal 2025 annual report showing EBITDA far below the USD 905 million of fiscal 2024, or third-quarter results showing net debt staying near USD 2,137 million after the seasonal working capital outflow reverses, would change the view.
Basis: calculation WC1; calculation DF1; calculation ND5; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 18, 36
### Limitations

- Trailing twelve-month EBITDA, cash interest and operating cash flow cannot be built because no fiscal 2025 annual statements are supplied, so leverage and interest cover are stated only at the year ends of fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2024.
Basis: calculation LT1; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 11
- Fiscal 2024 had 53 weeks, so growth and cover comparisons between fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2024 are not like for like.
Basis: 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 111

- Debt is stated at carrying value, net of issuance costs, while the company's own net debt is stated gross of them; the USD 29 million difference at August 2, 2026 is derived and not itemized in the quarterly report.
Basis: calculation RC1; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 12
- Maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not disclosed, so free cash flow here is operating cash flow less total capital expenditure.
Basis: calculation FC4; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 8

## Findings
### Bottom line

Sponsor and governance risk for creditors is medium: the former sponsor has held no shares since January 2024, but the company has funded sponsor-exit repurchases, acquisitions and growing buybacks partly from borrowings, and the covenants that would cap this are not supplied.
Basis: calculation SE4; calculation CR4; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 8

The operating base is diversified, with no customer above 1% of net sales in fiscal 2024, so the governance structure drives this view. Creditors face a recurring cash claim from the tax receivable agreements: USD 685 million is owed to former owners and the management holding vehicle, with USD 41 million expected within 12 months. In the second quarter of fiscal 2026 debt principal rose USD 318 million while the company repurchased USD 169 million of shares.
Basis: calculation TR1; calculation RF5; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1
### Key findings

No sponsor controls Core & Main, so no sponsor-driven distribution or sponsor equity support is documented in either direction. CD&R, the former sponsor, sold down through secondary offerings, seven of them between April 2023 and January 2024, and held no Class A or Class B shares from January 25, 2024. The company bought 28.05% of the shares those sellers disposed of in fiscal 2023, for USD 1,344 million. What remains is a classified board, Class A shares that are in many cases held through brokers and institutions (three holders of record at February 2, 2025) and the management holding vehicle's 3.30% of the combined Class A and Class B shares, held as Class B; larger current holders are not established because the proxy statement is not supplied.
Basis: calculation SE1; calculation SE2; calculation SE3; calculation SE4; calculation OW5; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 68, 75, 110

The sponsor exit was financed partly with borrowings, and it is the clearest case of cash going to shareholders while debt rose. In fiscal 2023, the year of the USD 1,344 million repurchases, net borrowings on the revolver rose USD 430 million and cash fell USD 176 million. A new USD 750 million term loan on February 9, 2024 repaid that revolver balance and named share repurchases among its permitted uses, so the exit financing became term debt; the revolver stood at USD 93 million at February 2, 2025 and was undrawn at February 1, 2026 and August 2, 2026.

Shareholder returns have grown and now exceed free cash flow, so leverage depends on earnings growth rather than debt paydown. In the first half of fiscal 2026 the company repurchased USD 257 million of shares and paid USD 42 million under the tax receivable agreements, USD 299 million in all against free cash flow of USD 112 million, while net new debt was USD 293 million. The authorization is USD 1 billion with USD 412 million unused at August 2, 2026, and a further USD 11 million was repurchased after the quarter end, so the pattern can continue. In fiscal 2024 acquisition spending was 4.21x repurchases of USD 176 million; in the first half of fiscal 2026 there were no acquisitions.

A USD 800 million term loan due 2033 and USD 750 million of 6.0% unsecured notes due 2034 repaid the term loan due 2028, so the first term maturity is now 2031. Debt principal rose USD 318 million in the second quarter and USD 320 million of the new borrowing exceeded the balance repaid; the offering notice named acquisitions and share repurchases among the uses and the quarterly report does not say how the excess was used. The notes rank equally in right of payment with other senior debt, while substantially all assets of the borrower secure the term loans and the revolver.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for lower risk is that the structure has been handled prudently: the company has no approved dividend plan, the revolver was undrawn at February 1, 2026 and August 2, 2026, three term loan repricings since May 2024 have cut the margin, final maturities now start in 2031, and the quarterly report states compliance with all debt covenants. If fiscal 2026 buybacks and tax receivable payments are met from operating cash flow rather than new term debt and the next annual report shows principal falling, the view would move to low. It would move to high if a new controlling holder appears, if the credit agreements show wide restricted-payment capacity that the company uses for larger debt-funded buybacks, if tax receivable payments accelerate, or if any amendment subordinates or releases lenders.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The latest financing closed on July 1, 2026, when a new USD 800 million term loan due 2033 and USD 750 million of 6.0% unsecured notes due 2034 repaid the term loan due 2028. Debt principal rose by USD 318 million in the second quarter, and USD 320 million of the new borrowing exceeded the balance of the old loan; the offering notice names general corporate purposes including acquisitions and share repurchases, and the quarterly report does not say how the excess was used.
Basis: calculation RF1; calculation RF3; calculation RF5; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 18; EX99.1_2026-05-03_cnm_jun2026seniornoteslaunchpr-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

Earlier steps moved maturities out in stages: a USD 750 million term loan due 2031 in February 2024, an increase of USD 200 million in December 2024, a revolver extended to 2031 in April 2026 and a margin cut on the 2031 loan from 2.00% to 1.75% in August 2026. The revolver was undrawn at August 2, 2026 and the company states compliance with all debt covenants at that date.
Basis: 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 79, 128; 10-Q_2026-05-03_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 19, 23

- Medium severity: The proxy statement is not supplied, so holders above 5%, board composition, committee membership and management incentive metrics are not established; Part III of the annual report is incorporated from it. - Medium severity: The tax receivable agreements are not supplied, so the acceleration formula and the schedule beyond 12 months are not established; only the recorded payable and the next 12 months are known. The action that would close it is the agreements and the issuer's payment schedule.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Core & Main's fundamental credit is adequate: USD 1,538 million of liquidity and no final maturity before 2031 support it, but shareholder returns now exceed free cash flow, so the creditor risk is leverage drift, not near-term liquidity.
Basis: calculation LQ1; calculation SR1; calculation FC4; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

On the last measurable basis net debt was 2.49x reported EBITDA at the end of fiscal 2024, and EBITDA covered cash interest 4.59x; the annual report for the year ended February 1, 2026 is missing, so trailing leverage cannot be stated. Net debt was USD 2,137 million at August 2, 2026 and USD 2,148 million pro forma for USD 11 million of repurchases made after that date, on a day the report does not state, about 2.23x the midpoint of the company's fiscal 2026 EBITDA guidance.
Basis: calculation LV2; calculation CV2; calculation ND4; calculation PF1; calculation GL2; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 5
### Key findings

Business risk is moderate: customers are highly diversified and capital needs are low, but demand follows construction. Tens of thousands of customers buy from the company, the top 50 are about 10% of net sales and the largest is under 1%; capital expenditure was 0.47% of net sales in fiscal 2024; and fiscal 2024 net sales of USD 7,441 million are 19.08% of a USD 39 billion market that management estimates. Against that, about 58% of sales go to private non-residential and residential construction on management's estimates, and the first half of fiscal 2026 sales grew only 1.27%, mainly through acquisitions.

Basis: calculation CX1; calculation MS1; calculation NM1; calculation GR2; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 14, 15, 86, 87; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 33; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Earnings have been flat while debt grew, which is why leverage is the issue. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 935 million in fiscal 2022, USD 910 million in fiscal 2023 and USD 930 million in fiscal 2024, a fall of 0.53% over two years, although the Adjusted EBITDA margin fell from 13.58% to 12.50% as SG&A rose 15.79% in fiscal 2024 against sales growth of 11.03%. Net debt rose from USD 1,877 million to USD 2,253 million in that year, taking net debt to reported EBITDA from 2.11x to 2.49x and cash interest cover from 8.47x to 4.59x.

### Company description

Core & Main distributes water, wastewater, storm drainage and fire protection products and related services to municipalities, private water companies and professional contractors through over 370 branches in the United States and Canada, selling more than 225,000 products from more than 5,000 suppliers to more than 60,000 customers. Fiscal 2024 net sales of USD 7,441 million are 19.08% of a USD 39 billion addressable market that management estimates, and the company names one other national competitor. The model earns about 27% of sales as gross profit by buying at scale and passing product costs to customers with a lag, and it links cash flow to repair and replacement of water infrastructure, to private construction and, for fire protection, to building projects; the business grew through acquisitions after a lineage that began in 1874 and a CD&R ownership from 2017 to January 2024.

For creditors the customer base supports cash-flow visibility, because no customer is above 1% of net sales and the top 50 are about 10%, and low capital needs (0.47% of net sales in fiscal 2024) help liquidity preservation. Revenue is not contracted, so debt service depends on construction activity and on the second-half release of working capital rather than on committed revenue, and refinancing confidence rests on the market access shown in July 2026.

Core & Main, Inc. is a listed holding company whose main asset is its interest in Core & Main Holdings, LP, which sits above the borrower, Core & Main LP. No holder is identified as controlling: CD&R, the owner from 2017, held no shares after January 25, 2024, the company repurchased USD 1,344 million of shares and interests from CD&R-affiliated sellers in fiscal 2023, and the management holding vehicle holds a non-controlling interest of 3.3%. The trend is stable operations with rising absolute debt, from net debt of USD 1,877 million at the end of fiscal 2023 to USD 2,137 million at August 2, 2026 (USD 2,148 million pro forma for USD 11 million of repurchases after that date), and the missing datapoints are fiscal 2025 EBITDA and cash interest, covenant calculations, the borrowing base and any rating.
Basis: calculation ND1; calculation ND4; calculation PF1; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

In the short term, 12 to 24 months, the only outlook the company gives is for fiscal 2026: net sales of USD 7,800 million to USD 7,900 million, Adjusted EBITDA of USD 950 million to USD 980 million (2.15% to 5.38% above fiscal 2024), a margin of 12.2% to 12.4% and operating cash flow at 60% to 70% of Adjusted EBITDA, and it reaffirmed this in September 2026. On the pro forma net debt of USD 2,148 million that is 2.19x to 2.26x, an indicator that supports the stable view if second-half cash flow of USD 426 million to USD 542 million arrives and buybacks stay near the first-half pace, but it is management's guidance, not an audited result.

Basis: calculation GL1; calculation GL3; calculation GL6; calculation GL7; calculation GL8; calculation GL9; calculation PF1; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 5; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Over three to five years the debt moves toward its first final maturities, the 2031 loan in February 2031 and the revolver in April 2031; the interest rate swap ends in July 2028, which leaves all USD 1,728 million of variable-rate debt unhedged, and tax receivable payments rise as exchanges continue (USD 41 million expected within 12 months against USD 42 million paid in the first half). Tailwinds are municipal demand and federal water funding, fire protection growth of 15.3% in the first half, and management's acquisition pipeline; headwinds are storm drainage volume down 2.9%, flat first-quarter sales on lower volume, tariff and petroleum cost uncertainty, and higher rates if the housing and commercial cycle weakens. Company-specific pressure comes from the repurchase pace, with USD 412 million of authorization left, which would add debt if free cash flow does not cover it.

### Qualitative downside scenario

The initiating condition is a downturn in private construction, which is about 58% of sales on management's estimates, coinciding with higher interest rates. The first operational break is volume: the first quarter of fiscal 2026 was flat on lower volume, storm drainage already fell 2.9% in the first half, and fire protection fell 13.37% in fiscal 2024. Revenue falls and margins follow because SG&A is sticky: each 1% fall in six-month sales removes USD 10.93 million of gross profit, and each point of gross margin lost is USD 40.55 million.

Basis: calculation NM1; calculation GR5; calculation SN1; calculation SN3; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 33; EX99.1_2026-05-03_cnm_cnmq12026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2

Free cash flow weakens, but the first-half working capital build of USD 242 million would shrink as receivables and inventory fall, which cushions cash; the borrowing base also shrinks with them, so availability under the USD 1,250 million revolver would fall by an amount that is not supplied. Liquidity of USD 1,538 million and near-term fixed claims of USD 58 million mean liquidity distress is unlikely in this scenario within a year; the exposure is leverage, because net debt of USD 2,148 million would sit on lower EBITDA and shareholder returns of USD 299 million in a half, if continued, add debt.
Basis: calculation WC1; calculation LQ1; calculation LQ3; calculation PF1; calculation SR1; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 18, 36; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Management has levers: buybacks, acquisitions and greenfield openings are discretionary, capital expenditure is small, and tax receivable payments are contractual but linked to taxable income. The refinancing consequence is limited before fiscal 2030 because the first maturity is February 2031, and the variable-rate cost rises by USD 17.28 million a year per percentage point once the swap ends in July 2028. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress; whether leverage stays acceptable depends on whether buybacks are cut in time, and the observable triggers are in the monitoring table.
Basis: calculation DS12; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 28; Business & governance (CP-1A)

### Overall credit view

Overall, Core & Main presents an adequate business profile supported by customer diversification, low capital needs and USD 1,538 million of liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by shareholder returns above free cash flow, USD 685 million of tax receivable claims and a leverage measure that can be fixed only to fiscal 2024. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because operating cash flow was 117.47% and 66.77% of Adjusted EBITDA in the last two fiscal years, although the first half is seasonally weak. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the leverage trend ahead of fiscal 2030, since no maturity falls before February 2031. The primary downside path is a construction downturn met with unchanged shareholder returns, which would raise leverage while liquidity holds. Against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector the business profile cannot be compared, because no peer data is supplied. Further analysis would require the annual report for fiscal 2025, the third-quarter report, the credit agreements and a rating or peer set. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: debt-funded shareholder returns ahead of a construction downturn.

## Gaps

- High severity: The annual report for the year ended February 1, 2026 is not supplied, so fiscal 2025 EBITDA, cash interest and operating cash flow are missing and no trailing leverage or cover can be stated; leverage is shown at fiscal 2024 and as an indicator on guidance. The action that would close it is that annual report or the third-quarter report.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 6

- Medium severity: The credit agreements, the borrowing base and the compliance certificates are not supplied, so covenant headroom, the revolver's true availability in a downturn and restricted-payment capacity are not measured. The action that would close it is the executed agreements and certificates.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 19, 36; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Medium severity: No credit rating, market spread or peer set is supplied, so the business and financial profile are not compared with other leveraged issuers and the notes' market pricing is known only through fair value at par. The action that would close it is rating reports and a peer benchmark.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 18

- Low severity: The fiscal 2026 outlook is management's guidance and gives no capital expenditure or interest guidance, so free cash flow and net debt at the fiscal year end cannot be projected from it; the implied second-half operating cash flow is arithmetic on guidance. The action that would close it is the third-quarter report.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation GL6; calculation GL7

- Low severity: The end-market split is a fiscal 2024 management estimate and the product category was renamed in 2026, and no contract length, renewal or churn data is supplied, so revenue durability is judged on customer breadth and category history. The action that would close it is the fiscal 2025 annual report.
Basis: 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 9; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 13

- Low severity: Maintenance and growth capital expenditure and the cost of the cost actions are not disclosed, so cost and capex flexibility is judged on total spending and the SG&A trend. No action closes this from the issuer's public statements.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 34

- Low severity: The latest supplied document is dated 2026-09-09, 70 days before the as-of date of 2026-11-18, and no third-quarter material is supplied; nothing after that document is used as fact. The action that would close it is the third-quarter report.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 48; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1
